title: Electrical Engineering, B.S. (Behrend)
notes: Penn State Erie, The Behrend College -- a genuinely separate curriculum from University Park's Electrical Engineering, B.S. (EE-2026.json), confirmed by direct bulletin comparison 2026-08-27: Behrend's own required EE sequence (EE 312, 316, 352, 360, 313W, 331, 387, 388, 453, 481, 400, 401) shares only EE 310/EE 453 by number with UP's own required set (EE 200, 210, 300W, 310, 330, 340, 350, 403W plus electives) -- Behrend runs its own ABET-accredited electrical engineering curriculum, not a 2+2 feeder. Built fresh (Pattern B) as EEBH per this session's new-major-code convention (UP code EE + 'BH'). Real 8-semester Suggested Academic Plan, 130 total credits, taken verbatim from the live 2026-27 Behrend bulletin page. 'Technical Elective (300/400-level)' (x3, Semesters 7-8) is wired to the bulletin's own Primary/Secondary structure (any 300-400 SWENG/EE/CMPEN course, any 400 CMPSC except 455/456, plus the enumerated Secondary list) via a merged match pool, same documented-approximation convention as CMPENBH-2026 (the real 'at least 2 primary / at most 1 secondary' ratio isn't independently enforceable by one match regex). Real-prereq-chain fixes: (1) CHEM 110 -> MATH 22 -> MATH 21 -- added MATH 21 + MATH 22 (Semester 1); MATH 3/4 not needed since MATH 21 has no real prereq (current convention, see EE-2026/CMPEN-2026's own notes). (2) The 'CMPSC 201 or 121' item is listed with CMPSC 201 first: CMPSC 201's real prereq is just MATH 140 (already done Semester 1), while CMPSC 121 separately needs MATH 110 -- letting the engine prefer 201 avoids an otherwise-unnecessary MATH-placement detour this major's own downstream EE 316 doesn't require (EE 316's real prereq accepts CMPSC 121/131/200/201 interchangeably). (3) REAL CATALOG GAP: EE 400's own live bulletin prerequisite (verified via a direct EE 400 search, not just the Behrend suggested-plan page) is 'EE 313W and EE 316 and EE 352 and EE 380 and seventh-semester standing' -- EE 380 (Introduction to Linear Control Systems) is a real course but never appears anywhere on Behrend's own EE suggested academic plan (Behrend's control-systems course for this curriculum is EE 481, a different course, already required separately in Semester 7). Rather than leave EE 400 permanently unschedulable or silently drop its real prereq, added EE 380 as an explicit extra item (Semester 5, Third Year Fall -- its own prereq, EE 312 or MATH 220, is already satisfied by Semester 4) so EE 400 -> EE 401's real chain actually completes; this adds 3 credits beyond the bulletin's own stated 130cr total (133cr), an intentional, documented gap-closing addition in the same spirit as ME-2026's MATH 3/4/21/22 additions, not a fabricated requirement.
